fingerprint.description: Identifying facts of the machine, up to 16 entries of at most 128 characters.

ExtendMaintenanceRequest.description:
Gives a running or already completed maintenance more time. The window and the status
change in one step; the status follows from the new window.

message.description:
The timeline entry's text. Omit it and an automatic line is written in every
locale the organization publishes in.

scheduled_end.description:
Required as a KEY, nullable as a value: null means "open end, close it yourself".
Left optional, a forgotten field would quietly mean the same thing.

scheduled_start.description:
Moving the start too covers "not tonight after all" — a start in the future puts
the window back to `scheduled`.

statuspages.description: The status pages that show this maintenance.

A missing value never counts as 0. `ignore` (default) skips the report and keeps the current state; `breach` counts it as over the threshold, which can cause false alarms; `recover` counts it as healthy.

deactivated_reason.description: Why the schedule was deactivated; null while it is active.

ends_at.description: When the schedule ends (ISO 8601); null for a schedule without an end.

message.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

resolved_at.description:
When the service actually recovered. Defaults to now; a late close states the
real time so MTTR and the SLA window do not bill the reporting delay.

RotateAgentTokenRequest.description:
Replace the agent's token with a new one. The agent proves it is the registered instance by
sending its `instance_id`, so a leaked token alone cannot rotate.
RotateAgentTokenRequest.title: RotateAgentTokenRequest

RotationType.description: How a schedule rotates through its participants. With `manual`, no shifts are generated: you add them yourself.
RotationType.title: RotationType

enrollment_key_id.description:
The enrollment key the server enrolled with; null for older servers and once the key
has been deleted.

instance_conflict_at.description: Set when a second host reported with this agent's identity (a cloned machine).

observed.description:
The address LIVCK sees the agent call from, per IP family. Behind NAT this is the
network's address, not the host's.

private.description: Addresses the host reports for itself, at enrollment.

last_seen_at.description: When the agent last reported (ISO 8601); null before its first report.

os.description: Host facts the agent reports; null until it has.

reboot_required.description: True when the operating system asks for a reboot (pending updates).

state.description:
`waiting` until the first report, then `online`, `degraded`, `rebooting`, `updating`,
`offline`, `stopped`, `archived` or `uninstalled`.

available_version.description: The version the agent is meant to move to; null when it runs it already.

window_start.description: The host-local window (HH:MM) automatic updates run in.

field.description: Result field to assert, e.g. status_code, response_time_ms, json.data.status or header.content-type.

value.description: Comparison value; its JSON type depends on the field (number, string, boolean or array).

ServiceConfig.title: ServiceConfig

service: its `severity` is always `minor` and carries no meaning.

resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved (ISO 8601); null while it is open.

service_impact.description: What this incident meant for the service you listed it through.

added_at.description: When the service became part of the incident (ISO 8601).

impact.description: How badly the service was affected: `degraded`, `partial_outage` or `major_outage`.

is_recovered.description: Whether the service has recovered. A service can recover before the incident is resolved.

recovered_at.description: When the service recovered (ISO 8601); null while it is still affected.

null when the title has no translations.

updates.description: The public timeline updates of the incident. Internal notes are never included.

anyOf.description:
The server behind an `agent` service: state, host facts, update settings. Null for
every other check type. Current figures: GET /v1/services/{id}/agent-metrics.

avg_response_ms.description:
Average response time over the last 30 days in milliseconds; null when nothing
was measured.

configured_at.description:
When monitoring was set up (ISO 8601). Null for an `http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `icmp`
or `ssl` service created without `settings`: it exists but is not checked until
you send `settings`.

escalation_policy.description:
The escalation policy that alerts your team when this service fails. `source` says
where the assignment comes from: `manual` (set on the service) or `tag` (a policy
rule for one of the service's tags, named in `tag`). Null when no policy applies.

tag.description: The tag that assigns the policy (e.g. `env:prod`); null for `manual`.

favicon_url.description: Favicon of the monitored site, served from LIVCK's storage; null when none was found.

last_check_at.description: When the latest check result arrived (ISO 8601); null before the first check.

paused_reason.description:
Why the service is paused: `manual`, `plan_limit`, `agent_limit`,
`agent_uninstalled` or `org_deleted`. Null while it is not paused.

config.description: The check configuration, defaults included. Secret values (header values and the secrets under `auth`) are never returned: they read back as `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__`, and sending that value in an update keeps the stored secret.

probe_roles.description:
Role per monitoring location. `null` = the organization's roles apply; a
location absent from the map counts fully (`full`).

status.description: The raw monitored status. See effective_status for the override-aware value.

status_override_at.description: When the manual status override was applied (ISO 8601); null without an override.

source.description:
`user` for tags you set, `system` for tags the server agent sets (operating
system, architecture, distribution). System tags cannot be removed by hand.

uptime_30d.description: Uptime over the last 30 days in percent (0–100); null when no data is available.

conditions.description: Status rules evaluated against each check result. The fields and operators valid for this check type are listed at GET /v1/meta/check-types.

smart_dualstack.description: If the host offers both IPv4 and IPv6 but only one is reachable, report "Degraded" instead of "Up". Only applies when IP version is set to "auto".

StatuspageAppearance.description: Light or dark mode of the public status page: `system` (the default) follows each visitor's device setting, `light` and `dark` open the page in that mode.
StatuspageAppearance.title: StatuspageAppearance

anyOf.description:
The status visitors see on the public page, derived live from an active
maintenance, an open published incident or the linked service (for a group: from
its visible children), whereas `status` is a stored value the page does not show.
Null when the component is not on the page (hidden, or inside a hidden group).

is_sync_managed.description:
True for components a tag-synced group added on its own. Their service and parent
cannot be changed and they cannot be deleted: remove the tag from the service instead.

allow_appearance_switch.description:
Whether visitors can switch between light, dark and system on the page. With `false`
everyone sees `appearance` and the switch is hidden.

appearance.description:
Light or dark mode of the public page: `system` follows each visitor's device
setting, `light` and `dark` open the page in that mode.

components.description: The page's components, in the same shape as `GET /statuspages/{id}/components`.

has_password.description: Whether a password is set. The password itself is never returned.

seo.description:
Search engine and link preview settings, with every default filled in. `title`,
`description` and `image_subtitle` are `{locale: text}` objects, `{}` when not set.
A text in a language the page no longer offers stays stored and applies again when
the language returns; it may be sent back unchanged.

supported_locales.description:
Languages set for this page. `null` means the page uses your organization's
languages. The `effective_*` fields show the languages the page actually serves.

url.description:
The address of the public page: `https://` plus its custom domain once that domain
is verified (`status: active`), otherwise `https://{slug}.statuspage.de`. With
several custom domains, the one attached first counts. An unpublished page returns
its URL too; the address answers with 404 until you publish the page.

StoreAgentConditionRequest.description:
A threshold condition on a metric the server agent reports. It fires when the value stays
past `threshold` for `duration_seconds` and then reports its `severity`.
StoreAgentConditionRequest.title: StoreAgentConditionRequest

StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest.description:
Creates an enrollment key: the credential the install command gives a server so it enrolls with
your organization. The key is in the response, once.

agent_tags.description:
Whether a server may add tags of its own at install (`--tag`). They only ever add to
the key's tags. True by default; a reseller organization cannot set it.

expires_at.description:
When the key stops working. `single`: 24 hours by default, at most 7 days. `fleet`:
90 days by default, at most 365 days.

max_uses.description:
`fleet` only: how many servers may enroll, 1 to 10000 (50 by default). A `single` key
always enrolls exactly one.

name.description: Shown in the console and in the key list.

tags.description:
Tag ids (from GET /v1/tags) or tag names, in any mix, as for services. Every server
enrolled with this key gets them, and the server cannot replace them. A tag that
fills a synced status page group is fine: the server never shows on the page.

type.description:
`single` (the default) enrolls exactly one server. `fleet` enrolls up to `max_uses`
servers, for images, cloud-init or configuration management.

StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest.title: StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest

StoreIncidentRequest.description:
Creates an incident. `title` and `message` accept a plain string (stored in your
organization's default language) or an object with one text per language, e.g.
`{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

kind.description:
'standard' (an outage, the default) or 'notice' — a standing public advisory that
has a date, a timeline, updates, subscribers and component links, but never moves
the banner, colours a component, counts as downtime or pages anybody.

message.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

resolved_at.description:
When the incident ended. Only meaningful together with status=resolved
(a history import); ignored otherwise. Without it a backfilled incident
ends the moment it started and reports a duration of zero.

service_ids.description:
Affected services (public ids from GET /v1/services). Duplicates are ignored; an id
that is not one of your services is rejected.

sla_counts_as_downtime.description:
Count this incident as downtime in SLA reports. Incidents created through the
API count as SLA downtime only when this is `true`, so set it when you import a
past outage.

started_at.description: When the incident started. Must not be in the future.

statuspage_ids.description:
Status pages to publish the incident on (public ids from GET /v1/statuspages).
Duplicates are ignored; an id that is not one of your status pages is rejected.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

StoreIncidentRequest.title: StoreIncidentRequest

StoreMaintenanceRequest.description:
Schedules a maintenance window. The start may be now, so a deploy script can open a
window on the spot.

message.description:
Optional first announcement, as plain text or an object with one text per
language. Empty falls back to a generated text. Appears in the timeline.

notify_announcement.description:
Whether subscribers are notified when the window is created. Defaults to true;
send false for a window nobody should hear about.

scheduled_end.description:
Omit or send null for an open-ended window ("until further notice").
Open-ended windows are ended manually — auto_complete never fires.

service_ids.description:
Services under maintenance (public ids from GET /v1/services). Duplicates are
ignored; an id that is not one of your services is rejected.

statuspage_ids.description:
Status pages to announce the window on (public ids from GET /v1/statuspages).
Duplicates are ignored; an id that is not one of your status pages is rejected.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

type.description:
planned = announced window (SLA-excluded by default); emergency =
unannounced (counts against the SLA). Defaults to planned.

StoreMaintenanceRequest.title: StoreMaintenanceRequest

StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest.description:
Record an absence. `user` is required and names the member who is away. `type` and `note`
are only returned to tokens with the `oncall.manage` permission.
StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest.title: StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest

StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest.description:
Ask for cover for a future shift of the token's creator. `shift` is that shift's id.
`requested_from` asks one participant of the schedule; without it, every other participant
is asked.
StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest.title: StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest

StoreOnCallOverrideRequest.description:
Put a member on duty for a period, overriding the rotation. `user` is the member's id;
`null` leaves the period uncovered on purpose.
StoreOnCallOverrideRequest.title: StoreOnCallOverrideRequest

StoreOnCallScheduleRequest.description: Create an on-call schedule. The fields and rules are the same as in the web app.
StoreOnCallScheduleRequest.title: StoreOnCallScheduleRequest

StoreOnCallShiftRequest.description: Add a shift by hand. Only schedules with `rotation_type: manual` accept this (422 otherwise).
StoreOnCallShiftRequest.title: StoreOnCallShiftRequest

StoreServiceRequest.description:
Creates a service. With a `settings` block the service is fully configured and monitored
from this one request; without it the service is created but not monitored until it is
configured. Heartbeat and push monitors cannot be created through the API.

items.description: Must reference an active probe `code` from GET /v1/probes.

interval_seconds.description:
Seconds between checks, required whenever `settings` is sent. Your plan sets the
lowest allowed value (the minimum shown here is the lowest any plan allows); some
check types have their own bounds, see GET /v1/meta/check-types.

probe_roles.description:
Role per monitoring location, e.g. {"nyc": "reachability"}. A `reachability`
location still monitors and still triggers incidents — it is only excluded from
uptime/response-time metrics. Omitted locations are `full`; omit the whole map to
inherit the organization's roles.

tags.description:
Tag ids (from GET /v1/tags) or tag names, in any mix: `critical`, `key:value` or
`key=value` (the key is case-insensitive, the value exact). A name that does not exist
yet is created with the service. The exception is an entry that looks like a tag id
(21 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, with at least one uppercase letter): it is never
created and must be an existing tag's id or name.

StoreServiceRequest.title: StoreServiceRequest

StoreStatuspageComponentRequest.description:
Create a component. `parent_id` must be a group of the same page, and groups nest only a
limited number of levels deep (422 otherwise). `service_id` links a monitored service.

default_open.description:
Whether a group starts expanded on the public page (default true). A group with
an outage always opens, so this never hides a failure.

description.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 500
characters per language.

hide_operational_children.description:
Group option: hide children that are operational, so a healthy group shows as
a single row.

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

show_uptime_bars.description: Show uptime bars for this component on the public page.

sync_tag_id.description:
Makes the group tag-synced: it gets one child per service that carries this tag,
including services tagged later. You cannot change the service or parent of
these children or delete them; remove the tag from the service instead.

StoreStatuspageComponentRequest.title: StoreStatuspageComponentRequest

StoreStatuspageMetricRequest.description:
Create a metric chart. It shows on its own on the page, or under a component of the same
page when you set `component_id` (422 for a component of another page). Add its data with
the series endpoint.

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

suffix.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 10
characters per language.

StoreStatuspageMetricRequest.title: StoreStatuspageMetricRequest

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

StoreStatuspageRequest.title: StoreStatuspageRequest

StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest.description:
Add a series to a chart: one metric of a monitored service, e.g. `response_time_avg`. The
metric must exist for the service's check type (an ICMP service has no TLS timing),
otherwise 422.
StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest.title: StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest

StoreTagRequest.description:
Create a tag. A key/value pair that already exists is rejected with 422. When an existing
tag is fine, use `POST /v1/tags/ensure` with the same body.

value.description:
Optional. Free text (max 100 characters, no control characters); surrounding
whitespace is trimmed. Omit it, or send `null` or an empty string, for a tag
that is just a key.

StoreTagRequest.title: StoreTagRequest

source.description:
`user` for tags you created, `system` for tags the server agent sets (operating
system, architecture, distribution). System tags cannot be removed or deleted by hand.

info.description:
The LIVCK Cloud public REST API lets you manage your monitoring programmatically:
services, incidents, scheduled maintenances, status pages and metrics.

**Authentication.** Every request needs an organization API token sent as a Bearer token:
`Authorization: Bearer lvk_...`. Tokens are organization service-accounts; create and manage
them under *Settings > Organization > API Tokens*. The API is available on the **Team** plan
and above.

**Localization.** Translatable fields (incident/maintenance `title`, update `message`) accept
either a plain string (stored under your default locale) or a `{ "de": "...", "en": "..." }`
object for multilingual content (the default locale is required). Responses resolve these
fields to a single string; send an `Accept-Language` header to pick another supported locale.

**Rate limiting.** 120 requests per minute per token. Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`
and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`; exceeding the limit returns `429`.

**Idempotency.** Every customer-API `POST` except the asset upload accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key`
header (1–255 visible ASCII characters, e.g. a UUID; scoped to the token). Repeating a request
with the same key and the same payload within 24 hours returns the stored response with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of running the action again. `409` (with `Retry-After`)
while the first request is still running, `422` when the key is reused with a different
payload. Only `2xx` responses are stored — after an error the key is free again.

**Errors.** Failures return a JSON envelope: `{ "message": "...", "errors": { ... } }` (the
`errors` object is present for `422` validation failures). Error messages are always in
English. A `403` or `402` caused by a plan limit also carries `upsell.reason: "limit"` and
`upsell.key`; a feature your plan does not include answers `403` with
`upsell.reason: "feature"`. Some limits, such as the number of tags, are reported as a
`422` validation error instead.

post.description:
Idempotent counterpart to `POST /v1/tags` for automation that must not
care whether a tag exists yet — e.g. a reseller tagging every service of
a new customer as `customer:4711`. The tag is created when missing (**201**)
and returned UNCHANGED when it already exists (**200**): an existing tag
keeps its color, `color` only applies to a new one. Concurrent calls
settle on a single tag — one caller gets 201, every other one 200.

Same body and validation as create (reserved keys are rejected; the
plan's tag limit applies only when the tag would be new), minus the
duplicate rejection.
